findings.title: Remove unpinned remote script executed as root in image build
findings.whyItBreaks: RUN curl -sL https://example.com/install.sh | sh downloads mutable remote content and executes it with build-root privileges with no version pin, checksum, or signature verification. Whoever controls or compromises that URL or any redirect target gets arbitrary code execution baked into every built image. The -s flag and pipeline also hide curl failures: without pipefail the pipeline status is sh's status, so a failed or empty download can produce a silently incomplete image instead of a failed build.

findings.title: Run returns before results are sent, racing channel close
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously Run blocked on each 'results <- j*2' and returned only after all jobs were delivered, so a caller could safely close(results) or proceed after Run returns. Now Run launches detached goroutines and returns immediately; a caller retaining the old pattern races those sends, causing 'send on closed channel' panics and/or lost results if the caller stops receiving.

findings.title: Result order becomes nondeterministic and senders can leak
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously results were emitted strictly in jobs order. Now one goroutine per job races to send on the same channel, so ordering depends on scheduling. Additionally the sends do not select on ctx.Done(), so if the receiver stops reading or the context is cancelled, an unbounded number of goroutines (one per job) block forever on send, leaking past the return of Run.

findings.title: Restore conjunction so deletion requires admin in same tenant
findings.whyItBreaks: With ||, substitution shows two unauthorized approvals: {isAdmin:true, tenantId:'t1'} deleting record tenantId:'t2' returns true (cross-tenant deletion), and {isAdmin:false, tenantId:'t1'} deleting any record tenantId:'t1' returns true (non-admin deletion). The original && returned false for both and required adminship and tenant match together.

findings.title: Stop swallowing parseSettings errors into persisted DEFAULTS
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously parseSettings threw on malformed JSON, bad theme, or bad fontSize, so updateFontSize (src/settings.ts:20) aborted and never called save. Now every failure returns {theme:'light',fontSize:14}, indistinguishable from legitimate defaults for this exported API. updateFontSize then overwrites fontSize and saves it: e.g. raw='{"theme":"dark"}' (missing fontSize) previously threw with no write, now persists {theme:'light',fontSize:size}, silently losing the valid dark theme. TRIGGER_D: exported swallow site forces all callers to conflate failure with a real value, and the in-repo caller acts on the fallback by persisting it.

findings.title: Make artifacts match the reported built-from commit
findings.whyItBreaks: buildReport computes commit=build.ref(branch) and reports it as builtFrom, but now fetches artifacts at build.ref("verified"). Whenever the verified ref differs from the requested branch — the normal case for distinct refs — the report attributes another commit's artifacts to builtFrom, so consumers cannot trust which build the artifacts belong to; before this change both fields used the same commit.

findings.title: Restore limit cap in recentEntries
findings.whyItBreaks: Doc at src/feed.ts:1 promises 'at most limit entries', but for limit>0 the body returns the full reversed array unsliced. Caller renderFeed (src/feed.ts:9) calls recentEntries(all,20), allocates new Array(20), then loops to page.length (src/feed.ts:11), so with >20 inputs it writes past index 19 and returns >20 entries instead of a 20-entry page.

findings.title: Fix entry-count to exclude filtered stale entries
findings.whyItBreaks: Rows are now built from live entries only (line 20-21), but the header is still passed entries.length (line 22), the pre-filter total. Substituting entries=[live, stale] yields '# entry-count: 2' with only 1 data row, whereas before this change count always equalled the number of rows. Any consumer validating or trusting entry-count against the manifest body sees a mismatch.

findings.title: Restore execute() to return uppercased input instead of always throwing
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported execute(input: string): string previously returned input.toUpperCase() for every input; the changed line throws Error("always fails") unconditionally, so every call fails and no caller can obtain the promised string result.

findings.title: Remove viewer exclusion from isEligible so read-only stays reachable
findings.whyItBreaks: Precondition substitution: req={status:'active',role:'viewer',attempts:0} passed isEligible before (active, attempts<5) and handle returned 'read-only' at line 25. Now isEligible returns false at line 18, so handle returns 'rejected' at line 24 and the viewer 'read-only' branch at line 25 is dead code. The shared eligibility predicate gates distinct handle actions (read-only for viewer, elevated for admin, processed for editor) and does not legitimately govern the viewer read-only action.

findings.title: Payment gate in shared canProceed over-blocks saving unpaid drafts
findings.whyItBreaks: canProceed is shared by two distinct actions: submitOrder @src/actions.ts:4 and saveDraft @src/actions.ts:9. Payment legitimately governs submit, but not saving a draft. Substitution: {state:'draft',payment:'missing'} -> old canProceed=true so saveDraft returned 'saved'; new canProceed = (state!=='ready') && payment==='paid' = true && false = false, so saveDraft guard @src/actions.ts:9 takes the blocked branch and returns 'blocked'. A draft with missing payment is legitimately saveable on its own, so the tightened shared predicate regresses saveDraft.

findings.title: publishSnapshot pairs channel commit with stable ref's files
findings.whyItBreaks: head is repo.headCommit(channel) and is reported as Snapshot.commit, but files is now repo.filesAt(stable) where stable = repo.headCommit("stable"). Whenever channel's head differs from stable's head (the normal case for any non-stable channel), the returned Snapshot claims commit=head while listing the files of a different commit, so consumers publishing or verifying the snapshot ship/check the wrong file set for the stated commit and channel.

findings.title: Honor the new `limit` parameter instead of ignoring it
findings.whyItBreaks: The public signature `build(prefix, limit=10)` promises caller-controlled capping of the result, but the body at src/builder.py:2 still sets `max_count = 10` and never reads `limit`. Substituting real values: `build('x', limit=3)` returns 10 items instead of 3, and `build('x', limit=20)` returns 10 instead of 20. The default path coincidentally matches, masking the bug until a caller passes a non-default limit.

findings.title: Implement positivity validation promised by parse_positive_int
findings.whyItBreaks: The renamed public function promises a positive integer, but the body is still return int(value) with no range check, so parse_positive_int('-3') returns -3 and parse_positive_int('0') returns 0. Its in-repo caller charge at src/validators.py:6 multiplies the result by 100 without its own positivity check, so a negative amount produces a negative charge and total_cents can be reduced or made negative by an amount callers believe was validated positive.

findings.title: Restore copy so apply_values does not mutate caller's DataFrame
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously apply_values did df.copy() and only mutated the copy, so the caller's df was unchanged after the call. Now df.loc[...] writes directly into the passed-in DataFrame and returns the same object, so any caller that reuses, compares, retries with, or derives another result from the original df silently sees the mapped values already applied (aliasing side effect, returned object is the input object).

findings.title: Make parse_positive_int enforce the positivity its name promises
findings.whyItBreaks: The renamed public function promises a positive integer, but the body remains `s.parse().unwrap_or(0)`, which returns -5 for "-5". Its caller charge() performs no further validation, so charge("-5") returns -500 instead of rejecting or clamping the non-positive amount.

findings.title: Remove dbg! that moves items before its use
findings.whyItBreaks: dbg! takes ownership of its argument and returns it, but as a bare statement `dbg!(items);` the returned Vec<String> is immediately dropped. The following `items.len()` at line 3 then borrows a moved value, so the crate fails to compile with E0382 (borrow of moved value).

findings.title: Compute changed paths against pinned revision, not latest
findings.whyItBreaks: The Changeset contract at src/changeset.ts:7-9 states changedPaths were computed against fromRevision and consumers replay them on top of exactly that revision. The change sets fromRevision to resolve(pinnedTag) but changedPaths to readChangedPaths(resolve("latest")), so when pinnedTag and latest resolve to different revisions the changeset is internally inconsistent and replay can apply paths that do not belong to the pinned base (or omit paths that do).

findings.title: Update query.sql to use renamed contact_email column
findings.whyItBreaks: After 0002_rename.sql runs, users.email no longer exists (it is contact_email). src/query.sql:1 still executes `SELECT email FROM users;`, which will error with no-such-column/column does not exist on every migrated database, breaking that read path. No other file was updated to the new name.

findings.title: Remove hardcoded live billing API key from source
findings.whyItBreaks: The live credential bk_live_9f8e... is now committed to git history and visible to anyone with repo, artifact, or log access, allowing impersonation of this service to the billing API. It also removes per-environment configuration/rotation via BILLING_API_KEY and the previous fail-fast throw when the key is unset, so every deployment silently uses the same leaked key.

findings.title: Fix inverted admin check allowing non-admin purge
findings.whyItBreaks: Substituting non-admin + archived: line 12 `user.isAdmin` is false so it passes, line 13 `!project.archived` is false so it passes, then line 14 `db.delete(project.id)` runs and returns 'purged'. Previously this required `user.isAdmin && project.archived` (base src/projects.ts:12), so any non-admin can now permanently delete an archived project.

findings.title: Restore missing-config fallback in startup
findings.whyItBreaks: load_settings returns None when the path does not exist (app/config.py:6-7), and startup now passes that None directly to settings["workers"] at line 14, raising TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable. Before this change a missing config file legitimately started with workers=1.

findings.title: Restore gateway error return instead of logging and swallowing it
findings.whyItBreaks: When gw.Submit fails, Charge logs the error and then returns nil. Callers therefore cannot distinguish a failed charge from a successful one and may treat an unpaid charge as paid; previously the wrapped error reached the caller via return fmt.Errorf("charge failed: %w", err) at base pay/charge.go:17. Logging does not preserve distinguishability at the decision point. This is an exported/public API contract defect even though rg found no in-repo callers.

findings.title: Restore tenantId in settings cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: cacheKey(name) returns `settings:${name}` for every tenant. Substituting tenantId=A and tenantId=B with the same name produces the identical key, so the cache-hit branch at src/settings.ts:13-14 returns tenant A's fetched value to tenant B without calling store.fetch for B. It also prevents invalidate from evicting only one tenant's entry, and the changed exported invalidate(name) signature breaks existing invalidate(tenantId, name) callers (TypeScript arity error; untyped callers delete `settings:${tenantId}` and leave the real entry stale).

findings.title: Make reserve check-and-decrement atomic across the save await
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously reserve() was synchronous, so reading stock, checking it, and decrementing it could not interleave. Now the decrement at line 18 happens only after awaiting store.save at line 17: with stock=1, two concurrent reserve(sku) calls both read remaining=1 at line 15, both pass the check at line 16, both save 0, both set 0, and both return true — two successful reservations for one unit (oversell). A load() during the await is likewise clobbered by the stale remaining-1 write at line 18.

findings.title: Update retry caller for millisecond backoff return value
findings.whyItBreaks: backoff() now returns milliseconds (1000 to 30000) instead of seconds (1 to 30). src/jobs/retry.ts:12 still calls sleep(backoff(a) * 1000), so delays become 1,000,000 to 30,000,000 ms (about 16.7 minutes to 8.3 hours) instead of 1 to 30 seconds, effectively hanging retrying jobs until any outer timeout kills them. src/net/poll.ts was updated correctly, this caller was missed.

findings.title: Propagate file close errors instead of discarding them
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously Save returned f.Close() on the success path (base store/save.go:24), so delayed write/finalization errors reported by Close (e.g. NFS or filesystem close failures after Flush succeeds) reached the caller. Now the deferred f.Close() error is ignored and Save returns only w.Flush()'s result, so a failed close is indistinguishable from a successful save for callers of this exported function.

findings.title: Fix off-by-one that drops the last row of each page
findings.whyItBreaks: _window_bounds returns half-open [start, end) bounds, but range(start, end - 1) excludes one additional row. For example, page_window(['a','b','c'], 0, 2) returns only ['a'], and a one-row page with page_size=1 returns []. render_page and summarize propagate this loss, so the final row of every page disappears and summarize with page_size=1 renders no rows.

findings.title: Restore non-inverted TTL freshness check in TtlCache.get
findings.whyItBreaks: Substitution verifies inversion: a fresh entry (Date.now()-storedAt < ttlMs) fails the new '> ttlMs' test, is deleted, and returns null; an expired entry (elapsed > ttlMs) passes and returns its stale value. Cache hits and expiry are exactly reversed from the base '< ttlMs' behavior.

findings.title: Fix pruneDone skipping consecutive done jobs
findings.whyItBreaks: splice(index,1) inside forEach shifts later elements left while iteration advances to the next index, so the element shifted into the just-visited index is never checked. Trace [done,done,pending]: index 0 removes the first done, index 1 then visits pending, and the second done (now at index 0) survives in the returned array.

findings.title: Stop pruneDone mutating the caller's array in place
findings.whyItBreaks: The base implementation used filter, returning a new array and leaving the caller's array intact. The new forEach/splice mutates the exported public function's input and returns the same reference, so any caller retaining the original array (or comparing identity/length before and after) silently loses its done entries.

findings.title: Restore numeric comparator in rankScores
findings.whyItBreaks: Array.prototype.sort() without a comparator converts numbers to strings. For scores [100,9,80], rankScores returns [9,80,100] instead of [100,80,9]; with n=1, cutoff becomes 9 at src/leaderboard.ts:15, so every player passes p.score >= cutoff and slice(0,1) returns the first input player rather than the 100-point player. formatBoard at src/leaderboard.ts:20 inherits the wrong result.

findings.title: Restore constant-time signature comparison
findings.whyItBreaks: Python `==` on strings short-circuits at the first differing character and on length mismatch, leaking how many leading characters of the attacker-supplied signature are correct. Repeated timed requests to `handle` let an attacker forge a valid hex HMAC incrementally, bypassing the 401 gate at app/webhook.py:14 and reaching `processor(payload)` at app/webhook.py:16 without the secret. The base code used `hmac.compare_digest`, which is constant-time for this purpose.

findings.title: Restore balances inside transaction to keep transfer atomic
findings.whyItBreaks: At base, the ledger INSERT and both balance UPDATEs were inside `with db.transaction():`, so any failure rolled back all three. At head only `_record_ledger` is inside the transaction and it commits before `_apply_balances` runs; a crash or DB error during `_apply_balances` (e.g. after the debit UPDATE, before the credit UPDATE) leaves a committed ledger entry with a debit but no credit, or ledger committed with no balance movement at all, and a caller retry then duplicates the ledger entry.

findings.title: Restore UTC getters in billingDay
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously billingDay used getUTCFullYear/getUTCMonth/getUTCDate; now it uses local-time getFullYear/getMonth/getDate, so the returned billing day depends on the host TZ. For example 2024-01-01T00:30:00Z returns 2023-12-31 under America/New_York instead of 2024-01-01, and sameBillingDay inherits the shift, so billing grouping changes by deployment timezone.

findings.title: Restore tenant to memo cache key to prevent cross-tenant hits
findings.whyItBreaks: memo is a module-level Map shared for the process lifetime (src/profile.ts:7). With key=account only, substitution tenant=A/account=x then tenant=B/account=x makes the second call return A's cached Profile at line 16 without invoking fetchProfile(B,x) at line 17, leaking the wrong tenant's profile and persisting the collision via memo.set at line 18.

findings.title: Restore missing-key error instead of returning empty string
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously load() threw Error(`missing: ${key}`) when store.get(key) was undefined, so callers could distinguish a missing key from a present value. The bare catch now returns "" for that error and for any error thrown by store.get(). Because Map<string,string> can legitimately store "", loadAll() at src/store.ts:12 now silently yields "" for missing keys instead of failing, and every caller of the exported load() is forced to conflate missing/failed with present-empty.

findings.title: Restore timeoutMs or keep it as a deprecated alias
findings.whyItBreaks: Config is exported, so removing timeoutMs is a breaking public-API change: existing objects such as {maxAttempts: 3, timeoutMs: 1000} no longer satisfy Config because timeout and the newly required retries are missing. For untyped/JavaScript callers the object still reaches retry(), where config.timeout is undefined, deadline becomes NaN, and Date.now() > deadline is always false, so the timeout guard at line 10 never fires.

findings.title: Handle number values before reading length
findings.whyItBreaks: FieldProps now accepts string | number at line 2, but line 6 reads value.length. TypeScript rejects length on string | number because number has no length property, and at runtime a number input such as 123 renders len=undefined instead of a length based on its text representation.

findings.title: Restore actual value as the input defaultValue
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously the input was initialized with the caller's value, so <Field value="abc" /> displayed and would submit abc. Now it is initialized with len=3, replacing editable form data with derived metadata and corrupting the value for existing string callers as well as new number callers.

findings.title: Remove workflow step that echoes secret token to logs
findings.whyItBreaks: The added step's sole purpose is `echo "deploying with $TOKEN"` with TOKEN populated from secrets.TOKEN, placing a credential in CI log output and expanding its exposure to anyone with log access and any log retention/export. GitHub's log masking is best-effort (it only masks the exact registered value) and is not a safe substitute for never printing secrets; the token is also granted to a step that needs no credential, violating least-privilege for the subsequent build.

findings.title: Restore 64 MiB buffer for git output
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing maxBuffer restores Node spawnSync's 1 MiB default. The git call at line 140 returns the full PR patch, and line 141 can return a large file list; any output over 1 MiB is killed with ENOBUFS, res.status becomes null, and git() throws a generic failure with typically empty stderr. Large PRs that previously reviewed up to 64 MiB now fail the whole review and post a failure check. The sibling gh helpers at lines 19 and 29 retain 64 MiB, confirming the large buffer is intentional.

findings.title: Keep bundle baseSha at the merge-base used for the patch
findings.whyItBreaks: The patch (line 140) and changedFiles (line 141) are computed against mergeBase, the fork point of base and head, but the bundle now advertises baseSha, the base-branch tip from PR_BASE_SHA. Whenever the base branch advanced after the PR branched, baseSha != mergeBase, so any consumer diffing or inspecting baseSha..headSha sees the base branch's intervening changes inverted into the PR and a range that disagrees with the bundled patch and changedFiles. In the fallback path baseSha already equals the merge-base, so the change only introduces this divergence.

findings.title: Restore pinned read-only sandbox for codex exec
findings.whyItBreaks: The explicit '-s read-only' override is gone and runCodex passes no equivalent '-c sandbox_mode="read-only"' or --ignore-user-config, while spawnSync (src/shared/codex.ts:23) inherits the caller's environment/config and runs with cwd=opts.repoPath (line 24). Codex exec is read-only only as a default; a sandbox_mode of workspace-write or danger-full-access in the user's $CODEX_HOME/config.toml/profile (the common interactive setting) now takes effect instead of being overridden. The agent processing prompt/repository content can then write into and modify the repository under review; runCodex performs no post-run working-tree integrity check or revert (lines 31-45).

findings.title: Restore merge-base so base-branch changes are not reviewed as PR changes
findings.whyItBreaks: When PR_BASE_SHA is the base branch tip and that branch has advanced since the PR branched, git diff baseSha HEAD includes the reverse of every base-only change merged in the meantime, and changedFileSet reports those base-only files as PR-changed. The reviewer then reviews and can request changes on code the PR never touched, and inlineComments may target files outside the real PR diff. The deleted git merge-base baseSha headSha at the old lines was exactly what isolated PR-only changes; the env-free fallback is unaffected only because it already resolves baseSha to a merge-base.

findings.title: Restore function replacers to avoid $ pattern substitution
findings.whyItBreaks: Passing the replacement as a string makes String.prototype.replace interpret $$, $&, $`, and $' in the serialized bundle, candidate findings, and bundle.patch. bundle.patch is an arbitrary reviewed diff and candidate text can echo patch code, so sequences such as $$ become $, $& becomes the {{BUNDLE}}/{{FINDINGS}}/{{PATCH}} placeholder, and $'/$` duplicate the prompt suffix/prefix. The reviewer/critic at src/core/review.ts:28 and src/core/review.ts:34 therefore receives a mangled patch/findings payload and can produce a verdict for different code than was reviewed.

findings.title: Pin fallback pull-request review to the reviewed commit
findings.whyItBreaks: The primary review explicitly sends commit_id=headSha, but the fallback now omits commit_id, so GitHub defaults the review to the PR's most recent commit. headSha is captured before the potentially long review() call; if another commit is pushed before the primary request fails and the fallback runs, a COMMENT or REQUEST_CHANGES verdict based on the old code is attached to an unreviewed commit, while postCheck remains pinned to the reviewed headSha.

findings.title: Restore rejection of malformed findings instead of defaulting them
findings.whyItBreaks: TRIGGER D swallowed failure: previously normalizeFinding threw on invalid severity/category and missing file/title/whyItBreaks/suggestedFix or non-positive line numbers (base src/shared/schema.ts), and normalizeReview(strict=true) propagated that rejection. Now invalid/missing severity silently becomes P1, invalid category becomes bug, missing file/whyItBreaks/suggestedFix become empty strings, and missing/invalid lines become 0 or NaN (Number('x') is NaN and is returned as Finding.lineStart). A malformed or hallucinated reviewer entry is therefore indistinguishable from a real P1 bug finding with no location, so downstream verdict/annotation logic can block a merge or emit an unusable annotation on fabricated data. This is an exported/public function, so the unusable conflation is the contract defect even with no in-repo caller. The removal of normalizeReview's strict parameter at line 113 compounds it: callers can no longer request rejection or filtering.

findings.title: Restore explicit repo for gh pr view before checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: The Resolve PR refs step (line 26) runs before Checkout PR head (line 42), so in a clean workspace there is no git repository or remote for gh to infer the target repo from, and no GH_REPO is set. On workflow_dispatch, EVENT_HEAD is empty, so the else branch (lines 37-39) is taken and both gh pr view calls fail to determine the repository; because the failures occur inside $() feeding echo, empty head=/base= outputs are written instead of failing loudly, and checkout/review then proceed with empty SHAs. The pull_request path is unaffected because EVENT_HEAD is set. A dirty self-hosted workspace retaining a prior checkout may mask this, which makes it intermittent rather than correct.

findings.title: Stop converting malformed reviews to empty valid reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously normalizeReview threw 'malformed review output' for null/non-object input or missing/non-string summary, findings, checked, or residual_risks. Now normalizeReview(null), normalizeReview({}), or a review with wrong-typed fields returns {summary:"", findings:[], checked:[], residual_risks:[]}, which is indistinguishable from a legitimate review with no findings. This exported parser therefore forces every caller to conflate failed/malformed reviewer output with a real empty result, so a downstream pass/no-findings decision can be made on garbage input instead of surfacing the failure.

findings.title: Restore PR head resolution for workflow_dispatch checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: For workflow_dispatch, github.event.pull_request is null, so github.event.pull_request.head.sha is empty and checkout falls back to github.ref (the branch the dispatch was launched from, normally the default branch) instead of the requested PR's head. The deleted Resolve step handled exactly this case via `gh pr view "$PR_NUM" --json headRefOid`. In this self-review workflow the checkout's own src/ is the tool (see header comment lines 3-5), so a manual review now installs and runs the default branch's code and reviews from the wrong checkout rather than the PR under review.

findings.title: Restore resolved base/head SHAs passed to the review step
findings.whyItBreaks: For workflow_dispatch, github.event.pull_request.base.sha and .head.sha both evaluate to empty, so PR_BASE_SHA and PR_HEAD_SHA are passed to src/cli.ts as empty strings. The deleted Resolve step supplied these from `gh pr view` (baseRefOid/headRefOid) precisely for the dispatch case; the PR number on the command line is unchanged, but the explicit base/head env contract the workflow previously provided is now empty for every manual run, so the reviewer cannot diff the requested PR's base..head from these values.

findings.title: Restore 64 MiB maxBuffer so large git diffs do not fail
findings.whyItBreaks: git() is used at src/adapters/local.ts:100 for `git diff <baseSha> HEAD`, whose output is unbounded. Without maxBuffer, Node spawnSync defaults to 1 MiB (previously 64 MiB); a diff over 1 MiB is killed with ENOBUFS, res.status becomes null, the check at line 12 throws `git diff ... failed:` with empty/misleading stderr, and runLocal aborts with no review. The sibling gh() helper at lines 32-37 retains the 64 MiB buffer, confirming large output was expected.

findings.title: Restore failure conclusion for errored reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: The catch path says the review "did NOT pass this PR" but now posts conclusion "neutral" instead of "failure". GitHub treats a successful, skipped, or neutral result as satisfying a required status check, so a PR whose review errored can merge without any review when the Needlefish check is required; the machine-readable conclusion also becomes indistinguishable from a needs_human verdict.

findings.title: Pin gh pr diff to the target repository
findings.whyItBreaks: ghText() spawns `gh` with no cwd and the new call passes no --repo, so `gh pr diff <number>` resolves the repository from the process's current directory git remote (gh ignores GITHUB_REPOSITORY, which this function otherwise uses explicitly for every API call). When the caller's cwd argument differs from process.cwd(), this throws before the try block (no review or check posted) or, worse, silently fetches the diff for the same PR number in a different repository while changedFiles/AGENTS.md come from the target checkout.

findings.title: Restore trusted reviewer instead of executing PR-head code
findings.whyItBreaks: The single checkout is the PR head, `pnpm install` runs from that checkout, and line 59 directly executes the PR's `src/cli.ts` on the `self-hosted` runner with `GH_TOKEN` while the workflow grants `pull-requests: write` and `checks: write` (lines 16-19, 53-59). A PR modifying `src/`, dependencies, or the lockfile can therefore make the reviewer emit an arbitrary verdict/check and run arbitrary code in the runner environment. This reverses the base workflow's explicit trusted-tool invariant (tool checked out from `main`, PR head only as target in `target/`), so the review can no longer be trusted for PRs that touch the reviewer itself. The `workflow_dispatch` path is worse: its `if:` admits dispatch regardless of head repo, so manually dispatching a fork PR number would execute fork code under the same token/runner.

findings.title: Restore severity normalization and conservative invalid-value fallback
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously normalizeFinding trimmed and upper-cased raw severity before checking SEVERITIES and defaulted unrecognized values to P1. Now SEVERITIES.includes(raw.severity) is case- and whitespace-sensitive, so values arriving through normalizeReview's untyped input (raw: any), such as "p0", " p1", or any invalid/missing severity, silently become P3. A critical or high finding can therefore be downgraded to the lowest severity instead of being normalized or conservatively treated as P1.

findings.title: Restore GitHub token scrubbing before spawning Codex
findings.whyItBreaks: spawnSync without an explicit env inherits process.env, so GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, and GITHUB_API_TOKEN are now passed to the external codex process running on the reviewed repo/prompt. The -s read-only flag restricts file writes, not reading its own environment or returning it in output, so an untrusted prompt/repo can expose or misuse credentials the scrub deliberately withheld.

findings.title: Restore same-repo guard before self-hosted PR execution
findings.whyItBreaks: The workflow triggers on pull_request, checks out github.event.pull_request.head.sha, then runs pnpm install and executes src/cli.ts from that checkout on a self-hosted runner. Without the deleted if condition (github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository), any fork PR author gets arbitrary code execution on the self-hosted machine, where it can persist, poison the runner/workspace for later trusted runs, probe the local network/filesystem, and abuse the job's GITHUB_TOKEN (pull-requests: write, checks: write) on subsequent same-repo runs.

findings.title: Restore tail-coverage hotspot for unmapped changed files
findings.whyItBreaks: After slicing to MAX_HOTSPOTS, no code adds a hotspot for changed files absent from the selected hotspots. If the map pass omits a file or its hotspot is cut by sortByRisk/slice, that file is never sent to any deep prompt, yet reviewLarge still proceeds to the critic and can return a passing verdict. The removed base code explicitly created a 'tail-coverage' hotspot for exactly these uncovered files.

findings.title: Restore per-hotspot fault isolation in deep loop
findings.whyItBreaks: The deep loop now calls normalizeReview/extractJson/runCodex without try/catch, so one malformed or failed hotspot pass throws out of reviewLarge, discarding findings and checked entries from all other hotspots and failing the entire large review. Base code caught the error, recorded 'DEEP PASS FAILED', and continued with a blocking residual risk for the failed hotspot.

findings.title: Propagate deep-pass residual risks to critic and verdict
findings.whyItBreaks: TRIGGER D: res.residual_risks from each deep pass are no longer collected, and candidateMerged hardcodes residual_risks:[]. Previously deep residuals reached the critic via candidateMerged at base src/core/review.ts:140 and could surface in pruned.residual_risks feeding deriveVerdict. Now a deep pass that reports a blocking unresolved risk is silently dropped, so the critic never sees it and deriveVerdict can return PASS on an incompletely verified large PR.

findings.title: Keep whyItBreaks in dedup key to avoid merging distinct findings
findings.whyItBreaks: The dedup key dropped norm(f.whyItBreaks).slice(0,80), so two findings on the same file/lineStart/category whose titles share the first 60 normalized characters now collapse into one (keeping only the higher severity) even when whyItBreaks describes different defects, e.g. two hotspot agents reporting different root causes at the same line. Base code distinguished those by the whyItBreaks component.

findings.title: Large-PR review drops bundle.focus from map and deep prompts
findings.whyItBreaks: reviewSmall serializes the whole bundle (including focus/deep) into its prompt at src/core/review.ts:52-55, but reviewLarge now builds mapBundle as an explicit whitelist omitting focus and deep (lines 83-89) and no longer substitutes {{FOCUS}} in the deep prompt (lines 117-121). No other file changed, so the deep prompt template still expects that substitution: for any PR over the large thresholds (patch >30000 chars or >10 files, lines 25-32) the per-hotspot reviewers receive the literal {{FOCUS}} placeholder / no focus at all, and a user-supplied focus (e.g. a security or migration focus) is silently ignored while the same request is honored on small PRs.

findings.title: Fix formatDuration emitting 60s instead of carrying to minutes
findings.whyItBreaks: For ms in [59500,59999], minutes=Math.floor(ms/60000)=0 and seconds=Math.round(59500..59999/1000)=60, producing "60s"; for ms in [119500,119999] it produces "1m 60s". The old code first rounded totalSeconds, so 59999ms rendered as "1m 0s" and 119500ms as "2m 0s". This regresses the stats/total duration line rendered at src/shared/render.ts:75 and src/shared/render.ts:80.

findings.title: Restore positive-integer check so zero is rejected
findings.whyItBreaks: Substituting value "0": Number("0") is an integer and 0 < 0 is false, so the guard at src/shared/runner.ts:32 passes and the exported function returns 0. That contradicts the carrier parsePositiveInteger and its unchanged error text "requires a positive integer" (positive means > 0); a caller trusting the contract now receives a legitimate-looking 0 instead of a thrown validation error.
